title: Coefficient comparison for compactly supported direct image
statement:
Let $f\colon X\to Y$ be a morphism of standing schemes, $f=p\circ j$ a
compactification ($j$ an open immersion, $p$ proper), so that $Rf_!=Rp_*j_!$
([sk-thm-existence] (2)), and let $\Lambda\to\Lambda'$ be a listed coefficient map. For
$K\in\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ the composite
$$
\gamma^!_{f,K}\colon(Rf_!K)_{\Lambda'}=(Rp_*j_!K)_{\Lambda'}\xrightarrow{\gamma_{p,j_!K}}Rp_*\bigl((j_!K)_{\Lambda'}\bigr)\simeq Rp_*j_!(K_{\Lambda'})=Rf_!(K_{\Lambda'})
$$
is an isomorphism in $\Dctf(Y,\Lambda')$. It does not depend on the
compactification and is compatible with the composition isomorphisms
$R(gf)_!\simeq Rg_!Rf_!$.

proof.text: For a compactification c, equip its middle scheme with the structure map c.g followed by Y.hom; properness makes this a standing scheme. Apply openExtension_constructible_finiteTor to K, using boundedness to choose its cohomological interval and finite Tor amplitude to choose its tensor interval. Thus c.i_! K belongs to Dctf. Apply scalarSixDirectImage (1) to the proper factor c.g. Its coefficient mate is invertible and its two endpoints belong to Dctf. The canonical open coefficient comparison is an isomorphism by derivedOpenImmersionShriekIso, so its proper pushforward is an isomorphism too. Their composite is precisely scalarCompactSupportMap. Transport the second endpoint properties across this isomorphism using constantModelConstructibleFiniteTor_wellDefined. This proves all three assertions of the first clause without the exceptional-image existence theorem or scalarSixCtf.

source.place: Isomorphism, Independence and Composition; T7 Lean assembly, 2026-10-26

proof.text: Apply scalarDenseRefinementSquare to the dense source d and the arbitrary boundary compactification c. That strictly smaller lemma pastes the square for a dense pair and the square for schematic-closure normalization. Unfold the pointwise compact-support comparison and erase identity associators: its conclusion is exactly the second clause of scalarSixCompactSupport.

source.place: Isomorphism, Independence and Composition; T7 Lean assembly, 2026-10-26

proof.text: Put the middle schemes of cf, cg, and cr over k using their proper structural maps; they are standing. The open immersions cf.i and cg.i are quasi-compact because the schemes are Noetherian. The proved properOpenInterchange_normalized theorem supplies existence and uniqueness of normalized pointwise interchange maps for both rings. The proved exists_interchangeNatTrans construction packages them into natural transformations; its biproduct argument proves naturality from the same uniqueness. Uniqueness identifies their values with the arbitrary normalized m and m-prime in the target. Apply scalarCompositeModelPasting. Finally identify the two open compositors: leftAdjointUniq after transporting the right adjoint equals the conjugate isomorphism, by the adjunction hom-equivalence and the unit-conjugacy identity. Consequently its model compositor and pointwise coefficient comparison are the original scalarCompactSupportModelComp and scalarCompactSupportMap. Substitute these equalities to obtain the entire third clause.
